I've used Spotify, Rdio and Google Music over the past few years. The battle for me is between Spotify and Google Music.

Spotify is really good at having curated playlists ready to go for almost every mood and genre, massive libraries that are easy to navigate on your desktop with a simple UI. There is also more of a social aspect you can take advantage of, whether it be following friends or your favourite musicians if they use the service too. I generally find more cool stuff on Spotify and it's much more geared for exploring music.

Google Music differs for me in that it's very easy to select a song, start a 'radio station' that makes a playlist of usually decent songs that I can then quickly choose to save as a playlist to my phone and listen to on the go. If you really like a song, giving it a thumbs up will give Google's algorithms a better idea I'd what you're into and when you use the I'm feeling lucky button it will usually give you a themes playlist based on a given song. Google Music will also let you upload 10,000 songs from your own library as well, this is nifty if you'd like to save some space and download them again later.

Personally, I chose Google Music. Spotify keeps songs in your collection and ones in playlists separate, so you can only listen to one set of songs or the other if you haven't made sure to double save all those. Spotify is much better for exploring new music, but I found Google Music did a pretty decent job putting together lists anyway.

I hope that helps!

The time I kept working at my job when my company was having financial troubles and was slow to pay people.

The company I work for was very healthy. Commissions were high (I am not in sales, but I do work with the numbers), margins were healthy and deals were rolling in. The deals started trickling down and everyone thought it was the slow season. It's been a year now, and it still isn't what it was. The margins are more and more thin, every deal comes with an argument over commissions, suppliers are not as willing to give us breaks. It isn't a fast drop - the company is just bringing in less and less new revenue and is losing a little more every month. Still very profitable, but it has definitely gone down. Many of the new deals coming in are re-terming existing customers at lower rates - often just by squeezing profit margins. Every deal that comes in comes with a battle with the suppliers to the point where every deal has special rates. They've hired 2 people to add structure to the organization and formalize processes and another person to assist. The former were both let go after a couple months and the latter was moved to another position. The provisioning and support office lost half its employees and everyone left in that office and companywide are disillusioned with the company and the industry in general, all the way from the top down. Add in that the owners are all at odds with one another when they used to be good friends.

To make a really long post end abruptly - I am getting the hell out of there.
